fields.label: Skills Data
fields.format: A JSON list as text of skill ids, e.g. ["alchemy", "handleAnimals", "pickLock"]: camelCase, as the sheet's skill groups spell them. Plain text is refused, because the sheet would show nothing

fields.label: Languages Data
fields.format: A JSON list as text of language names, e.g. ["Caelian", "Variac"]

fields.label: Hover
fields.format: Foundry works this figure out and reports it, so never invent one

fields.label: Save Threshold
fields.format: Foundry works this figure out and reports it, so never invent one

fields.label: Kit Details Data
fields.format: A JSON list as text holding one object per kit the hero carries (a tactician carries two), each the kit's bonuses: `name`; `meleeDamageT1`, `meleeDamageT2`, `meleeDamageT3` and the same three for `ranged`; `meleeDistance`, `rangedDistance`; `stability`, `speed`, `stamina`, `disengage`

fields.label: Potency (weak)
fields.format: Foundry works this figure out and reports it, so never invent one

fields.label: Potency (average)
fields.format: Foundry works this figure out and reports it, so never invent one

fields.label: Potency (strong)
fields.format: Foundry works this figure out and reports it, so never invent one

fields.label: Abilities Data
fields.format: A JSON list as text, one object per ability, as Foundry reports it: `name`; `type` (main, maneuver, freeManeuver, move, triggered or freeTriggered); `category`; `cost`; `keywords` (a list of words); `powerRollChars` (a list of characteristic keys); `trigger`; `effects`, the rules text, one entry per block with `description`, `before` (true above the power roll) and `type` (`spend` adds `resource`), which older Foundry versions send as `effectBefore` and `effectAfter`. Leave `tiers` out: it is Foundry's own nested effect list

fields.label: Features Data
fields.format: A JSON list as text, one entry per feature: its name, or an object with `name`, `description` and `level`

fields.label: Perks Data
fields.format: A JSON list as text, one entry per perk: its name, or an object with `name` and `description`

fields.label: Titles Data
fields.format: A JSON list as text, one entry per title: its name, or an object with `name` and `description`

fields.label: Treasures Data
fields.format: A JSON list as text, one object per treasure: `name`; `category` (leveled, trinket, consumable or artifact); `echelon`; `quantity`; `keywords` (a list of words); `description`

fields.label: Conditions Data
fields.format: A JSON list as text of condition ids, e.g. ["bleeding", "prone"], or objects with `name` and `severity`

fields.label: Organization
fields.format: One of minion, horde, platoon, elite, leader or solo. The published formulas read it, so a creature without one gets no formula figures

fields.label: Role
fields.format: One of ambusher, artillery, brute, controller, defender, harrier, hexer, mount or support. Leave it out for a leader or solo

fields.label: EV
fields.format: Leave it out on a new creature: the published formulas give it from level and organization, and the stat block editor fills it in, marked as the formula's, when the director opens Edit stat block and saves. Never estimate it; where no published formula covers the creature it stays for the director. Write it only to set a number the director gave you

fields.label: Stamina
fields.format: Leave it out on a new creature: the published formulas give it from level, organization and role, and the stat block editor fills it in, marked as the formula's, when the director opens Edit stat block and saves. Never estimate it; where no published formula covers the creature it stays for the director. Write it only to set a number the director gave you

fields.label: Winded
fields.format: Leave it out: it is half the creature's Stamina, rounded down, and the stat block editor sets it with Stamina

fields.label: Immunities
fields.format: Comma text, e.g. "fire 5, poison 3"

fields.label: Weaknesses
fields.format: Comma text, e.g. "holy 5"

fields.label: Movement
fields.format: Comma text of special movement, e.g. "fly, climb"

fields.label: Free Strike
fields.format: Leave it out on a new creature: the published formulas give it from level, organization and role, and the stat block editor fills it in, marked as the formula's, when the director opens Edit stat block and saves. Never estimate it; where no published formula covers the creature it stays for the director. Write it only to set a number the director gave you

fields.label: Traits
fields.format: A JSON list as text, one object per trait: `name` and `description`

fields.label: Abilities Data
fields.format: A JSON list as text, one object per ability: `name`; `type` (signature, action, maneuver, triggered or free); `keywords` (comma text, e.g. "Melee, Strike, Weapon"); `distance` (e.g. "Melee 1", "Ranged 10", "3 burst"); `target`; `power_roll` (the bonus, e.g. "+3"); `tier1` (11 or lower), `tier2` (12 to 16), `tier3` (17+), each the result text with potency written in it, e.g. "6 damage; A<2 prone"; `trigger` (triggered abilities); `effect`; `spend_vp` and `spend_effect` for a Malice spend; `auto_damage: true` on an ability whose tiers open with damage, so the stat block editor sets that damage from the published formula and keeps the words after it

fields.label: Villain Actions Data
fields.format: A JSON list as text of up to three villain actions, leaders and solos only: `name`; `order` (opener, crowd-control or ultimate); then the ability keys `keywords`, `distance`, `target`, `power_roll`, `tier1` to `tier3`, `effect` and `auto_damage` as for abilities

switch.label: treasure fields
switch.summary: Type, Kind, Echelon, Keywords, Effect, the three levels and how to make it

fields.label: Type
fields.format: One of Consumable, Trinket, Leveled or Artifact

fields.label: Kind
fields.format: Leveled treasures only: Weapon, Armor, Implement or Other. Leave it out for any other type

fields.label: Echelon
fields.format: Consumables and trinkets: 1st, 2nd, 3rd or 4th. Leveled treasures and artifacts have none

fields.label: Keywords
fields.format: Comma text, as the book prints them, e.g. "Magic, Potion" or "Heavy Weapon, Magic"

fields.label: Effect
fields.format: What the treasure does. A leveled treasure leaves it out and uses the 1st, 5th and 9th level fields

fields.label: 1st level
fields.format: Leveled treasures only: what it does at 1st level

fields.label: 5th level
fields.format: Leveled treasures only: what changes at 5th level

fields.label: 9th level
fields.format: Leveled treasures only: what changes at 9th level

fields.label: Needs
fields.format: The item prerequisite: what a crafter needs before the project starts

fields.label: Lore from
fields.format: The project source: the texts or lore a crafter learns it from

fields.label: Project roll
fields.format: The characteristics the project roll may use, e.g. "Reason or Intuition"

fields.label: Project goal
fields.format: The project goal as the book prints it, e.g. "45"

widgets.name: Monster Builder
widgets.description: Edit a creature's stat block in place, with your party, the encounter budget and completeness checks beside it. Figures follow Draw Steel's published formulas until you change them. On a Creature page, use Edit stat block instead; placed elsewhere, it builds a new creature.

widgets.name: Creature Stat Block
widgets.description: The creature's stat block, shown under the title of every Creature page, with Edit stat block and Publish for the director. Chronicle mounts it itself.

widgets.name: Bestiary
widgets.description: Creatures from this campaign and the Draw Steel book: rows that open the stat block in place, roll buttons, hover cards and a reference tray

config.label: Layout (full, or compact for a block on a page)
Show creatures from (all, campaign or book)
Only these creatures (names or book ids, comma separated)

widgets.name: Character Sheet
widgets.description: Full Draw Steel character sheet for hero pages. Mounts on drawsteel-character pages and on any character-preset category, through the manifest's renderers.

widgets.name: Rulebook Front Page
widgets.description: The dynamic rulebook's editorial front page — hero Power Roll block, characteristic cards with fold-out wings, condition flap rows, and the Lich's Lair worked-scene hub. Best placed on a campaign dashboard or a dedicated 'Rules' page. Inside a Handbook page it shows only the Lich's Lair, as a pop-up book.

widgets.name: Negotiation Tracker
widgets.description: Runs a Draw Steel negotiation on an NPC page: interest and patience, motivations and pitfalls, arguments and a log. Players see only what the GM chooses to show.

widgets.name: Negotiation Audience
widgets.description: A pop-up book for the Handbook's Negotiation chapter: a cut-paper throne room where the reader picks who speaks and what they say, rolls, and watches the king's interest and patience move by the published rules (read from data/negotiation.json).

widgets.name: Handbook Credits
widgets.description: The Handbook's Credits chapter: a cut-paper stage where the eleven classes in white masks take a bow, the MCDM team by role (read from data/credits.json), where to buy the books, the Creator License notice word for word, and a film-style credits roll over the whole window with pause and fast forward.

widgets.name: Class Fights
widgets.description: Pop-up books for the Handbook's Classes chapter: a tile per class with its Heroic Resource, and for each class a cut-paper practice fight where the reader clicks the pieces and watches the resource rise and fall by that class's rules (read from data/class-fights.json).

widgets.name: Encounter Budget
widgets.description: The Draw Steel budget panel inside Chronicle's encounter builder: the party's encounter strength, the EV spent against the published difficulty bands, the guideline checks and each initiative group's EV. Chronicle loads it itself; there is nothing to place.

renderers.description: Full Draw Steel hero character sheet on the Hero entity show page (bespoke drawsteel-character slug).

System-agnostic binding: render the Draw Steel hero sheet on ANY entity type whose preset_category is 'character' (e.g. a 'hero' or 'character' slug type adopted by the player-character addon), not only the bespoke drawsteel-character slug.

text_renderers.name: Rules References
text_renderers.description: Resolves {@category term} syntax to styled tooltips with Draw Steel rule definitions. Chronicle loads it as a global before the package's widgets.

text_renderers.name: Monster Engine
text_renderers.description: Encounter math for the monster builder, evaluated through the DrawSteelFormulas section of monster-engine.js. Loaded as a global before widget scripts; no visible UI.

text_renderers.name: Monster Party
text_renderers.description: Pure party read + PartyProfile derivation for the monster builder. Loaded as a global before widget scripts; no visible UI.

text_renderers.name: Rulebook Fold Engine
text_renderers.description: Reusable, content-agnostic fold-interaction module (hinged wing / rotateX flap / FLIP reader takeover, with dismissal priority, viewport clamp, sibling dim, deal-in, face-down search, reduced-motion, plus glossary hover/tap cards). Loaded as a global before widget scripts; consumed by rulebook-frontpage. No visible UI of its own.

text_renderers.name: Rulebook Example Player
text_renderers.description: Reusable, content-agnostic staged-example player: character tokens slide in and glow, lines light one by one, the roll ticks its dice, settles, steps the math out with its why, and the tier stamps on; ↻ replay; reduced-motion reveals instantly. Scripts are data (data/rulebook-examples.json). Loaded as a global before widget scripts; consumed by rulebook-frontpage. No visible UI of its own.
